note: R20 difficulty pass off tools/sim-emberveil.mjs (300 seeded runs, seed 1, cross-checked on seeds 2-5). Round 20 gave every zone a settlement (shop + cleric revive) and took fast travel away, so a party can always walk back to a healer: fights per run went from ~55 to ~88 and full six-act clears rose to 38.3% against the user's target of 10-15%. This pass rebuilt enemies.actMultipliers from act 2 up, trading enemy HP for enemy damage so late fights hit harder without dragging (act 6 is 17.7 rounds instead of 19.6), stretched the top of the XP table so the level cap is not reached until act 6, and trimmed the gold multiplier. Result: 12.3% clears on average over five seeds, act 1 at 86-88%, and a funnel that loses roughly 13/20/25/29/39/44 percent of the runs still standing in each act. Previous note (R19): the XP curve was the fault - the party hit the level cap in act 5 and finished act 6 holding three times the XP the table asks for, so heroes outgrew every enemy multiplier; that pass stretched the XP table, trimmed XP and gold, lifted acts 1/4/6, added a per-act armour ramp and magic resist, and made bosses scale with the trash around them. Previous note (R14): act 2 was the wall - softened act 2, smoothed the act-2->3 HP step, lifted hero skill damage, and tuned hunger and torches. NG+ Act 1 uses the highest-act enemy multipliers (enemyScalingForNgPlus shifts effectiveAct = min(10, act + 4*ng)).

progression.note: R20: the last five steps were stretched (level 26-30 now cost 60k/74k/92k/118k/150k, up from 58k/68k/80k/94k/110k). With a settlement in every zone the party banks far more XP than it used to: at the head of act 6 it holds ~183,000 XP, which was 170% of the old level-30 cost - it hit max level in act 5 and coasted through two acts with nothing left to earn. At the new numbers it is level 27.5 entering act 5 and 29.8 entering act 6, so levelling (and the full heal that comes with it) is still a live reward in the last third of the game. R19: the table runs to level 30 and climbs much faster after level 10. statPointsPerLevel and passivePointEveryNLevels are NOT read from here yet - js/main.js hardcodes +2 attributes and every 5th level - so changing them would split the live game from the simulator. xpTable and talentPointLevels are live.

skill.note: M399: per-category split (heavy/light/magic). magicMult 0.78 brings spell damage about 22% under their pre-split numbers so spells stop dealing 4x basic-attack damage; bumping heroDamageMult 0.82 -> 0.95 keeps melee/ranged where they were after the M382 solo-viability fix, since the magic-only nerf carries the spell-rebalance load now.

mitigation.note: M207: both live + simulator run the WoW-style curve DR. DR = min(cap, armor/(armor+k)).

globalMultipliers.note: R19: unchanged. The per-act table below carries the difficulty now, and `armor` here is multiplied by the per-act `armor` figure.

actMultipliers.note: Per act: HP and damage multipliers, an armour multiplier applied on top of globalMultipliers.armor, and a flat magic-resist top-up (almost every enemy template has 0 magic resist and two thirds of hero damage is skills). R20: acts 2-6 were rebuilt against the settlement-in-every-zone map. Damage climbs faster than HP from act 3 on - the same lethality in a shorter fight, which kept the funnel where we wanted it and cut act 6 from 19.6 rounds a fight to 17.7. Act 1's HP multiplier being higher than act 2's is not a mistake - these scale each act's own templates, and act-1 monsters have a fraction of the base HP act-2 monsters do.

ngPlus.note: M382: hpBase 1.35→2.5 and dmgBase 1.25→1.7 so NG+1 Act 1 actually feels like late-game combat. Combined with the act-shift (NG+1 Act 1 uses Act 5's actMultiplier), enemy effective HP is roughly Act 5 baseline × 2.5 in NG+1.

boss.note: A boss's HP multiplier is 1 + (actHpMult - 1) * hpShare, so it scales more gently than the trash around it. hpShare was hardcoded at 0.35 in rules.js makeEnemy; at act 6 that made a boss scale 1.65x while a trash mob scaled 2.85x. 0.5 keeps bosses a step behind the curve without making them a speed bump.

champion.note: Chance is `chance + perAct * (act - 1)`, so champions go from 1 in 20 in act 1 to 1 in 10 in act 6.

named.note: How often an ordinary node turns into a named leader with followers, and how much stronger that leader is.

partySize.maxNote: Round 21 (E38): how many heroes walk in the active party. Extra hires wait on the bench, and Manage Party (in a settlement) swaps them within this limit. Read by js/bench.js partyLimit().
partySize.note: M382: enemy damage scales with party size so a solo run isn't four-times harder than a four-hero run. Companions are NOT counted toward party size for this lookup — only heroes.

companions.note: M380: companions gain these attribute bonuses per (effective level − template level). Pairs with Companion Level Sync so an L1 War Dog hired in Act 1 actually scales into late game.

globalMultipliers.note: R20: gold 1.1 -> 1.0. A party reaches act 6 with more gold than it can spend (~24,000, against a best-in-shop item well under 5,000); the trim costs nothing measurable in clear rate (12.0/14.0/13.3% on seeds 1-3 with it, 11.7/13.0/13.7% without) and takes the act-6 purse down to ~21,000. It is a dent, not a fix - the surplus mostly comes from selling loot, so a real economy pass would have to look at dropRate and loot.sellPrice. xp stays at 2.2 (round 20 cut it from 2.85 when the settlements went in). shopPrice marks up what a merchant asks without changing what he pays you for your leftovers (loot.sellPrice divides it back out); dropRate scales every zone drop.

loot.note: R19: affixMult scales every rolled affix value (items.json keeps the ranges); uniqueChance scales the per-boss unique odds in items.json bossLoot. R22 (E49): setChance is the share of ZONE DROPS that come out as a set piece - it is rolled only after a kill already dropped something (loot.zoneDrop), so the R19 value of 0.025 meant about 0.4% per kill: 0.18 set pieces in all of act 1 over 100 simulated runs, which is why nobody ever saw a set. 0.18 gives roughly two to three pieces per act. classSetShare is how often a set drop is picked from the sets of the classes in the party (loot.partyClasses) instead of any set of the act's tier.

services.note: R22 (E47): town services. Every action costs gold (times the item's rarity factor), is capped, and shows its result before the gold is spent. Blacksmith: raise an item's quality one step (damage, armour, block and barrier scale with qualityMult), up to maxQualityByAct for the act you are in. Enchanter: add a property to a free affix slot (slots per rarity: normal 0, magic 2, rare 4, legendary 6), reroll one property into a different one (cost grows by rerollGrowth each time the same item is rerolled, up to maxRerolls), or raise rarity one step (gold + the listed material). The result of add and reroll is fixed by the item's own enchant seed, so the preview is exactly what you get.

affixes.note: existing affix ranges are in src/game/items.js per-act tables (AFFIXES_ACT1..AFFIXES_ACT5). Baseline leaves these in code; tuning knobs in economy/enemies sections cover the target range for M4.

curveDr.note: Shipped in M207 via combat.mitigation.curveDr + liveFormula='curve-dr'.

world.note: Round 20: the travel layer Emberveil 2 added is tunable from here (js/game.js reads it). Night raids are the main risk of sleeping on the road.

nightRaid.note: A night raid is harder than the same fight in daylight (extra = extra bodies on top of the vehicle modifier, hp/damage multiply the raiders) and pays more (xp/gold multiply the win, dropChance is an extra roll on the zone drop table).
